# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment
The incumbent is timing-feasible at 40 LUTs, 90 FFs, WNS 0.456 ns, and WHS 0.086 ns, so iteration 1 must improve the LUT objective while retaining both timing gates. The top’s numeric latency is unknown; no numeric top annotation is required, and its observable cycles must remain unchanged. No prior trial outcomes are available.

## Hypothesis
Replacing the arbiter’s variable-index cyclic search and winner-based input mux with fixed one-hot priority equations and masked input selection may reduce LUT use by removing dynamic index and selection logic.

## Instruction for generator
In `rr_arbiter4`, replace the `candidate`/`k` loop that indexes `req[candidate]` and the `case (winner)` address/data mux with explicit cyclic priority equations derived from `last`, producing a one-hot winner and using it to select `addrN` and `dataN`. Preserve the registered grant, write enable, address, and data outputs; synchronous reset values; idle-cycle zero outputs; and the rule that `last` holds when no request is present. Keep the top interface and all observable cycle behavior unchanged, and retain this candidate only if it passes every gate and strictly improves the LUT objective against the verified incumbent.
